open_points.subject: AllocationInstruction and ExpenseAllocation precision
open_points.text: M26 and M27 say allocation amounts are “otherwise unconstrained”, the carried change says validation checks “only the sum”, and M29 stores the amount “as instructed”; the modeling convention and A9 instead require every stored monetary amount to have exactly 2 fraction digits.
open_points.question: May an allocation with more than two fractional digits be accepted and stored when the allocation list sums exactly to the expense total, or must each allocation independently satisfy the 2-digit money rule?
options: Accept and store arbitrary-precision allocation amounts because only their sum and targets are validated.
Reject any allocation amount that is not a 2-digit EUR amount.
Round each allocation half-up before checking the sum and storing it.
open_points.default_guess: Reject each allocation amount with more than two fractional digits; do not round operator instructions.

witness.initial: An active project has a valid EUR expense total of 10.00.
events: An authorized operator submits allocations of -0.001 to section A and 10.001 to other_expenses; their exact sum is 10.00.
outcomes: Under M26/M27 and the carried validator description, the instructions are accepted and those exact amounts are stored.
Under the modeling convention and A9, the instructions are refused because neither stored amount has two fraction digits; alternatively an implementation may round them before storage.
witness.observer: The operator sees acceptance versus refusal, and later staff and viewers see different allocation values and section totals.

open_points.subject: Inbound monetary precision
open_points.text: A9 says “Decimal, 2 fraction digits, ROUND_HALF_UP at derivation boundaries; stored amounts are already 2-digit exact,” but it does not say whether an inbound amount with a different scale is rejected or normalized before storage.
open_points.question: At each monetary input boundary, what happens to finite Decimal values with fewer or more than two fractional digits?
options: Require at most two fractional digits, reject excess precision, and normalize accepted values to two digits.
Round every inbound value to two digits using ROUND_HALF_UP before later validation.
Require exactly two digits in the submitted representation and reject values such as 10.0 as well as 10.005.
open_points.default_guess: Accept values with at most two fractional digits and normalize them to two digits; reject excess precision rather than rounding operator or source facts.

witness.initial: An active project exists and has no manual section plan yet.
events: An authorized operator submits a manual section plan with material_planned = 10.005 and work_planned = 0.00.
outcomes: The boundary rounds 10.005 half-up and stores 10.01.
The boundary treats 10.005 as an invalid EUR amount and refuses the plan without storing anything.
witness.observer: The operator sees success with 10.01 versus a refusal, and viewers may later see the rounded plan.

open_points.subject: Overall progress precision
open_points.text: A9 defines overall progress as “Σ(work_planned × percent) / Σ(work_planned)” and calls it a Decimal, but it gives no scale, precision, or rounding point for a non-terminating quotient; the 2-digit rule is stated for money.
open_points.question: How is overall_progress_percent represented and rounded when the weighted division has no finite Decimal result?
options: Round the final percentage to two fractional digits with ROUND_HALF_UP.
Use a separately specified percentage scale and ROUND_HALF_UP policy.
Expose whatever precision the implementation's Decimal context produces.
open_points.default_guess: Round the final percentage to two fractional digits using ROUND_HALF_UP.

witness.initial: The active budget has section A with work_planned 1.00 and recorded progress 0%, and section B with work_planned 2.00 and recorded progress 100%.
events: A viewer or authorized staff member requests the progress view.
outcomes: The view reports overall_progress_percent as 66.67 after explicit two-digit half-up rounding.
The view reports a longer context-dependent Decimal approximation such as 66.66666666666666666666666667, or another chosen scale.
witness.observer: The viewer or staff reader sees a different progress value, and serialized responses differ across implementations.
